items.author: sheriff_ayinla
items.context: @sheriff_ayinla (4.565 seguidores), en inglés: «No blockchain exploit. No contract bug. $282M stolen after fake wallet support tricked a victim into revealing 12 seed words. Verify alerts on the project's own channel. Never share your seed. Test small first.» Noticia de hackeo fresca, con ~1 min de publicada y 0 respuestas. Ángulo: custodia (la semilla como superficie de ataque y la firma air-gapped).
items.suggested_text:
This is the part most security advice skips: the strongest wallet in the world can't protect a seed its owner hands over. $282M with no exploit and no bug means the attack surface was a person and a support chat, not the cryptography.

A useful rule of thumb: the 12 words have exactly one legitimate use, restoring a wallet you control on a device you set up yourself. No support team, firmware update or "verification" flow ever needs them. Setups where the seed never touches an internet-connected device make that rule easier to keep, because there's nowhere convenient to paste it. Example of an air-gapped signer: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2116083014815924397

Phishing keeps getting more convincing. The habits that stop it have barely changed in a decade.
